speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. I understand you are presenting with a breast mass; to better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have noticed this lump and if it is painful or changing in size?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: A 48-year-old woman with a rapidly growing, painful breast mass over four weeks. Have you noticed any skin changes, dimpling, nipple retraction, or discharge from the affected side? Also, do you have a history of breast cancer in you or your close family members?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: This patient's presentation is inconsistent with gastroenteritis, which affects the gastrointestinal tract; her symptoms of a rapidly enlarging breast mass require urgent evaluation for malignancy or other breast pathology. I am requesting a breast ultrasound and mammogram immediately to assess the mass characteristics.
